What goes into building a padel court?
Everything you don't see
Everyone sees the glass, the turf, the clean lines. Here's what has to happen first.

Step 1: Design and planning
Site evaluation · Court orientation · Designs · Permits
First, design and planning. We evaluate the site, set the court's orientation, produce the designs, and pull permits: structural drawings, local approvals, and zoning.

Step 2: Ground preparation
Level · Compact · Drainage
Then ground prep: leveling the site, compacting the soil, and installing drainage. Rush this and the court has problems later.

Step 3: Foundation
6" post-tensioned concrete slab
4,000 PSI minimum · Integrated slope and drainage
Next, the foundation: a six-inch post-tensioned concrete slab, at least four thousand PSI, with slope and drainage built in.
Same slab question as the dimensions video: post-tensioned (page) vs rebar (FSC brochure). Video follows the page unless you change it.

Step 4: Steel structure
Steel frame and mesh panels
Hot-dip galvanized for outdoor courts
The steel frame and mesh go up. For outdoor courts we recommend hot-dip galvanized steel to prevent corrosion. Tolerances are tight because the glass has to fit exactly.

Step 5: Glass panels
1/2" tempered safety glass
Half-inch tempered safety glass goes into the frame. Fit and alignment matter: gaps change how the court plays.

Step 6: Turf and net
Padel turf: 1/2" pile, 9,000 Dtex, sand infill
Net tensioned to regulation height
Then padel-specific turf with sand infill, cut and tensioned so the ball bounces true. The net goes in at regulation height.
Keep the sand type generic (no grade on screen).

Step 7: Lighting
High-efficiency LED · Even coverage, no glare
LED lighting gives even coverage without glare, and it's what keeps a court in use after five p.m.

Step 8: Finishing touches
Court markings · Accessories
Last, the markings and accessories that turn a construction site into a place you want to play.
